reviews.author: YJ Oh
reviews.text: A famous Japanese crockery store in Seongsu-dong. Although the interior is not very large, it is eye-catching with colorful products on display. The store is located on the first and basement floors, and there are a wide variety of pretty and cute ceramic dishes and kitchen accessories on display. It is said that almost 100% of the products are imported and sold from Japan. It's good to be able to purchase small items such as drinking glasses, paper cups, and spoon rests individually. When I listened to the story of the store staff, it was said that they had been selling imported crockery only wholesale for three generations and started selling it at retail not long ago. They say they deal directly with local kilns in Japan, but the prices don't seem to be that cheap. It appears to be a store frequented mainly by young people, and people who run Japanese restaurants are also said to visit frequently. There are two stores in operation in Seongsu-dong alone, and this is the first store. I think it's a unique store that you can go to just to look at the pretty dishes. There is no separate parking space, but it seems possible to park for a while in the resident priority parking area on the side of the road, and it would be a good idea to use a public parking lot nearby.

Myeongryun Son Kalguksu and Hyehwa Kalguksu in Hyehwa-dong, and Miryang Son Kalguksu in Donam-dong are Seongbuk-dong restaurant-style kalguksu restaurants opened independently by people who worked in the kitchen of Seongbuk-dong Guksi Restaurant.
However, I have been to Seongbuk-dong Guksi House, which is said to be the original, and have eaten Myeongryun Kalguksu and other restaurants, but in my personal opinion, the place that I think offers the most delicious and luxurious meat broth-based kalguksu restaurant is Seongbuk-dong Restaurant..!
The taste of the kalguksu is the best, but the kimchi that comes with it, the young radish kimchi, is also really good, and the taste of the geotjeori kimchi made by soaking and grinding dried red peppers in water is also excellent.
The taste of the broth, with its delicate, luxurious meaty aroma, is also the best. The homemade noodles are hand-sliced and the light dumplings are also the best.
The price is a bit expensive, but in terms of taste, there are few kalguksu restaurants like this restaurant, so it is by far the best meat broth-based kalguksu restaurant.

reviews.text:
I never thought this house would still be alive.
If I recall, it was a restaurant that insisted on not using seasoning. We wanted to confirm the authenticity of the taste from our customers. The prices were hotel-level, but the ingredients were similar to those at popular restaurants. Still, it seems like the basics of material management were followed.
However, stubbornness ruined the taste. How absurd it was when the owner said, “We don’t even use salt, just season it.” After the owner left us, the food cook came carefully and asked us how it tasted. I still regret that I should have told you honestly when I asked.
At one time, there was a wellness boom in the food industry and there was a huge trend of stigmatizing chemical seasonings. Some PD's broadcast further encouraged it. No salt, no sugar. When I think about it, I think it was a transitional period that occurred in the process of the restaurant industry growing in a new direction at the time. It wasn't necessarily a bad thing. There must have been great people who focused on good ingredients and combination methods to create good taste. But in the end, to use good ingredients, freshness is the key, to guarantee freshness, turnover must be supported, and to obtain turnover, accessibility, quality, service, and cleanliness must be met. This store didn't fit all of that.
Neither fine dining nor restaurants can survive without turnover, but they can survive if the business owns its own real estate. Living with pride, not with restaurants, that is probably one of the ways of the world.

reviews.text:
■ Seoul’s first traditional tea house

Suyeonsanbang has been the home of Heosang Lee Tae-jun since the 1930s and is currently designated as a folk cultural property.

Sangheo Lee Tae-jun is a pioneer of modern short stories in Korea. During the Japanese colonial period, this place served as a living room for many writers, and his granddaughter opened it as a hanok cafe in 1998.

As Suyeonsanbang is the first traditional cafe in Seoul, it is so famous that it is crowded with locals and foreigners on weekends.
Therefore, the first thing you need to do as soon as you arrive is to record the wait.

Parking is available for about 5 cars in front of the cafe.

This Suyeonsanbang restaurant has been introduced so many times that it has never been featured on TV restaurant introduction programs.
It was also introduced in Wednesday Gourmet and Gourmet Heo Young-man’s Baekban Travels.

The Korean and Schisandra chinensis, especially the red bean shaved ice, are the best I've ever had.
Even my wife, who doesn't like red bean shaved ice very much, enjoyed it.

Hangwa is a free service for one person.
If you ask for more, they give you more.
The taste of Korean sweets is also the best.

The exterior shape of the house and the garden appear to have remained intact.
You can enjoy tea in the main body, annexes, the floor, and throughout the yard, but the yard is dark due to mosquitoes.
However, if you want, you can ask for mosquito repellent and they will give it to you.

If I were to find a downside to Suyeonsanbang, the prices on the menu are all high.

However, if you sit on the veranda and look down at the garden while feeling the breeze blowing from the large fan, your eyes and mind will be refreshed.

There is a restroom on the first floor, a place with a good view of the outdoors, and a lot of people visit.
The 1.5th floor has dark long tables, and on the other side, there are many high-ceilinged seats with a warm wooden atmosphere.
The ambiguous space on the 1.7th floor was made into a dark and secret space, like a warehouse space.
The second floor was spacious and nice, but it felt noisy due to the sound echoing.

The interior is decorated with concepts such as silkworms and thread decoration, and is quite charming.

It is said that he participated in Donghak during his childhood, but his father, who was from a government office, tried to dissuade him, causing conflict, and he became a monk. He had a wife and a son from his marriage before becoming a monk, but the son defected to North Korea, and later, while teaching at Seonwon, he married again and his daughter, whom he gave birth to, is said to be alive today.

reviews.text:
This is where Manhae Han Yong-un, one of the 33 national representatives during the March 1st Movement and the poet of ‘Your Silence,’ lived from 1933 to 1944.
Han Yong-un was a monk who tried to reform Joseon Buddhism, an independence activist who worked hard for his country's independence, and a poet who left great achievements in modern literature.

Ilsong Kim Dong-sam (1878-1937) was the leader of the anti-Japanese armed struggle in Manchuria and an independence activist who led the Korean Declaration of Independence and the National Unification Party movement.
He was arrested by the Japanese police in Harbin in 1931, suffered imprisonment, and died in Seodaemun Prison in April 1937.
Manhae Han Yong-un collected his body and held a five-day funeral at Simwoojang.
The funeral, which was held under strict surveillance by the Japanese, was also attended by Cho Heon-yeong and Cho Ji-hoon.
